fixes.explanation: That's what happens, baker. Ruth 1:18 says, "When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her." Once Naomi sees how set Ruth is, she lets it go. I think Ruth's mind was made up harder than a day-old cookie.

Moab it is, baker. The text says a man from Bethlehem went with his wife and two sons "…to reside in the land of Moab." (Ruth 1:1). Leaving home for another country is a big move, and I think it took real nerve. I get nervous just moving my cookie boxes to a different shelf.

Edom is a fair guess, but it's not where this family lands. The text says the man from Bethlehem went "…to reside in the land of Moab." (Ruth 1:1). Good guess, baker, I've guessed worse on a map with no labels. Moab is the name to hold onto.

Rachel is a fair guess, but it isn't the name here. Ruth 1:4 says the sons took Moabite women as their wives, "…one named Orpah and the other named Ruth." Those are the two names this story gives us. Ruth is the one to hold onto, baker.

Dinah is a fair guess, but the text doesn't name her here. Ruth 1:4 names the two women: "…one named Orpah and the other named Ruth." I have a feeling Ruth's name is going to keep turning up in this story, like chocolate chips in a good batch. Hold onto it, baker.

True. Naomi tells them, "May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband." (Ruth 1:9). She names rest, a home and a husband for each of them. I think that's a kind thing to say on a hard road, especially while they're all weeping.
Mara. Naomi says, "Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me." (Ruth 1:20). She's asking for a new name to go with how she feels. I think this part is heavy, and it hurts.

Naomi says it the other way around, baker: "I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty." (Ruth 1:21). Full going out, empty coming back. I think she's telling the women of Bethlehem how it feels.
Wheat is a good guess, but this verse names a different grain. Ruth 1:22 says, "…they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest." Barley, baker. Wheat just has to sit this one out.
